newsitem.title: UK: Lockerbie lawyer doubts Libyans will be tried.
newsitem.headline: Lockerbie lawyer doubts Libyans will be tried.

text.p: The Scottish lawyer of two Libyans suspected of bombing Pan Am flight 103 over Lockerbie with the loss of 270 lives said on Sunday he did not expect his clients ever to be brought to trial.
Alastair Duff told Sky News television he believed the authorities in Scotland and the United States were unwilling to make the compromises necessary for the case to reach court.
"My gut feeling is that there will never be a trial. I see no signs of the U.S. or Scottish authorities backing down over the issue of the venue for the trial," Duff said.
"If I have not made it clear thus far, I make it clear again: my clients are not going to change their position.
"I do not believe that Colonel Gaddafi (the Libyan leader) will force them to leave Libya."
On Monday Duff is speaking at a London conference of the International Bar Association, which is calling for the creation of an international court to try such cases.
The bombing of flight 103 over the Scottish town of Lockerbie in December 1988 killed 270 people in the jumbo jet and on the ground.
In 1992, the two Libyan suspects were indicted by Scottish and U.S. legal authorities, but they have refused to surrender themselves for trial.
Sanctions were imposed on Libya because of Colonel Muammar Gaddafi's refusal to hand the men, Abdel Basset Mohammed Al-Megrahi and Al-Amin Khalifa Fhimah, over for trial.
Libya insists that it will only hand over the men to what it calls a fair and just international court.
British officials said it remained the government's policy that the two Libyans should be handed over to face trial.
